name: Arousal Regulation Circuit
short_description: Monitors current arousal level against optimal setpoint, modulated by stimulus complexity, to generate approach-avoid signals and behavioral adjustment.

components.name: AROUSAL_SENSOR
components.description: Monitors autonomic arousal indicators including heart rate, skin conductance, and respiratory rate

components.name: SETPOINT_COMPARATOR
components.description: Compares current arousal to optimal arousal setpoint for context

components.name: COMPLEXITY_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Assesses stimulus complexity to modulate optimal arousal target

components.name: DRIVE_CONTROLLER
components.description: Translates arousal discrepancy into approach-avoid motivation and behavioral direction

key_references: Berlyne, D. E. (1971). Aesthetics and Psychobiology. Appleton-Century-Crofts.
Yerkes, R. M., & Dodson, J. D. (1908). The relation of strength of stimulus to rapidity of habit-formation. Journal of Comparative Neurology and Psychology, 18(5), 459–482.
design_implications: Optimal arousal increases with task complexity (Yerkes-Dodson); provide appropriate challenge level—high-complexity tasks need lower baseline arousal, simple tasks tolerate higher arousal
Overstimulation and understimulation both reduce engagement; design spaces with variable complexity to accommodate different arousal preferences and temporal variation
